comparator.sourceNotes: The programme pages (s1, s2) describe the structure in words only: a common first year, a second year of electives, skills and projects, and a third year with one of four concentrations and a thesis; they give no course list with EC. The 180-EC reconstruction therefore uses the 2026-2027 Education and Examination Regulations (s0): Article 3.6 (study load per year), 3.7 (core), 3.8 (electives), 3.9 (concentration and thesis) and Appendix I (course overview). Year 1: eight mandatory 5-EC courses, 10 EC of skills courses and two 5-EC projects. Year 2: eight elective 5-EC courses and four elective 2.5-EC skills courses (two courses and one skill per period, chosen from the published framework) plus two mandatory 5-EC projects; the framework is availability-dependent, so one coherent valid selection linked to the Circular Chemical Engineering concentration is instantiated (Organic Chemistry, Fluid Mechanics, Numerical Methods, Polymeric Materials, Differential Equations, Biochemistry, Heat & Mass Transfer, Remake Reuse Repair Recycle; skills in organic chemistry, statistics, fabrication and design, and analytical and physical chemistry) and is flagged here as an instantiation of restricted choice rather than a fixed requirement. The Heat & Mass Transfer elective is explicitly linked to this concentration, which satisfies the requirement that one elective be linked to a third-year concentration. Year 3: one mandatory 5-EC core course (Ethical and Philosophical Reflections), the Circular Chemical Engineering concentration of five 5-EC courses (the fifth, Circular Process Design and Control, shown in the period 3-4 slot) and two 2.5-EC skills courses, and the 25-EC bachelor thesis (BTH3010). Totals are 60 EC per year and 180 EC overall.

routeSelection.basis: The target is the generic bachelor and its third year offers four formal concentrations (Circular Chemical Engineering, Sustainable Biotechnology, Engineering Physics for Sustainable Manufacturing, Sustainable Mechanical Engineering), none of which is shown by current official evidence to be more representative of the programme's broad identity or less specialised than the others. The official curriculum page and the 2026-2027 Education and Examination Regulations list Circular Chemical Engineering first, and its year-1 chemical-engineering core and year-2 Heat & Mass Transfer link make it a coherent continuation of the common curriculum, so the neutral order tie-break selects it. The route was not chosen by reference to UCR course fit.

exception.reason: The defining curriculum of the selected route is a chemical-engineering sequence built on physics and chemistry: Fundamentals of Engineering, Chemistry and Chemical Engineering, and Thermodynamics and Engineering Physics in the compulsory first year, physics, electronics, chemistry and biology laboratory skills, fluid mechanics and heat and mass transfer in year 2, and in year 3 chemical engineering thermodynamics and kinetics, separation processes, reactor engineering, chemical plant design, process design and control, unit-operations and industrial-process-design skills and a 25-EC engineering thesis. UCR offers circular-economy, life-cycle, energy and environmental-engineering-adjacent courses, a mathematics and numerical-methods line and biochemistry and cell-biology courses, but no physics, chemistry sequence, thermodynamics, transport phenomena, reactor or process engineering, mechanics or engineering design. A 24-course programme would be a sustainability-and-mathematics programme with a small circular-economy core padded with unrelated life-science or computing courses, and it would not reproduce the programme's engineering substance; the unmatched components include essentially all of the 25-EC concentration course sequence, the engineering physics and chemistry core and the thesis. The comparison would have to present adjacent sustainability courses as substitutes for engineering content that UCR does not teach.
exception.curriculumContext: The 2026-2027 regulations define a 180-EC curriculum of 60 EC per year: year 1 has eight compulsory 5-EC courses, 10 EC of compulsory skills and two 5-EC projects; year 2 has eight elective 5-EC courses and four 2.5-EC elective skills courses chosen from a published framework plus two 5-EC projects; year 3 has one 5-EC core course, a concentration of five 5-EC courses and two 2.5-EC skills courses, and the 25-EC thesis. Of the four concentrations the neutral order rule selects Circular Chemical Engineering. The year-2 electives are an instantiated valid selection of restricted choice; no open free-choice space beyond that framework is published and none is fabricated.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 course rows in the current enriched UCR workbook, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, prerequisites and planned terms. Relevant adjacent offerings are ENSSUST112 Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy (life-cycle assessment and circularity), ENSDELT311 R3: Recycling, Recovery, Remediation (circular-economy strategies with laboratory skills and inorganic chemistry), ENSSUST211 Energy & Sustainability and ENSSUST311 Renewable System Design (energy systems and technical-economic assessment), ENSDELT111 Building with Nature, DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus (multivariable calculus and differential equations), DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems, DISDATA312 Robotics, HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry and HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory. They give partial counterparts to Engineering in a Circular Economy, the Life Cycle Assessment Project, Calculus, Linear Algebra, Multivariate Calculus, Numerical Methods, Differential Equations, Biochemistry and Biotechnology, but none to Fundamentals of Engineering, Chemistry and Chemical Engineering, Thermodynamics and Engineering Physics, the physics, electronics and chemistry laboratory skills, Fluid Mechanics, Heat & Mass Transfer, the five-course Circular Chemical Engineering concentration with its skills courses, the design projects or the thesis. No course in the workbook covers physics, thermodynamics, chemical or process engineering, reactor or separation technology, or mechanics, so these isolated adjacent offerings cannot support a coherent 24-course Circular Engineering programme.
